en:
Wait a moment.
If I'm telling the fourth story, there's no need to go all the way back to the newspaper club.
The story I meant to tell is about this cherry tree, too.
...My name is Akemi Iwashita.
I'm a third-year.
I must say, my heart skipped a beat when Fukuzawa chose the cherry tree for the third story.
I couldn't believe that a first-year like you would know a story about this cherry tree.
After all, this story was a legend known only to a very select few.
...But I'm glad.
Glad that Fukuzawa's story was a lie.
Wherever did you hear that story about this cherry tree?
Some of it may well be accurate, but what on earth did you hear that let you make up a story like that?
Perhaps you have a gift for writing fiction, Fukuzawa.
Or are you simply a swindler?
...Please don't be angry with me.
I'm only telling the truth.
This place was a dumping ground for corpses during the war, you say?
This cherry tree was forced to watch horrifying sights, over and over, you say?
During the war, they threw living people away along with the dead?
That is ridiculous beyond words.
Besides, even if it were true, there are countless sights far more horrifying than that.{p}

After all, they say this cherry tree is more than a thousand years old.
That much, I'll grant.
This area, you see, is famous for a great battle fought here in the Warring States period.
Have you studied your history?
Do you know what people with hardly any food ate to stay alive in the Warring States period?
...I'd rather not say it myself.
And do you know what kind of life they were forced to lead?
Stripping the armor and helmets off dead warlords and trading them for a pittance, peeling the scalps off heads and selling the hair, hunting down defeated samurai who had survived and ganging up to beat them...
Was all of that just a dream, I wonder?
Those heaps upon heaps of corpses back then must have given this cherry tree all the nourishment it needed to grow, don't you think?{p}

Heh heh...
If that were how it worked, every tree in Japan would have to be cursed.
No one could ever go cherry-blossom viewing.
Someone would have to die every time anyone set foot in a forest.{p}

It's true that this cherry tree is steeped in a grudge.
Many grudges, in fact.
But they don't belong to the soldiers who died in the war, nor to the warlords who died in the Warring States period.
It's something else...
They're grudges born of the fierce, wicked attachment that people living perfectly ordinary lives felt for this world.
{a}{f:|}?
What you saw a little while ago was that grudge.
Not the soldiers who died in the war.
Now I'll tell you the truth.
The story of the real grudge that has taken hold of this cherry tree.
In return, will you make me a promise?
No matter what happens, you won't move from this spot until my story is over.
And you will never, ever scream.
Understood?{p}Can you promise me that?
I can promise
I can't promise

I'm so glad you promised me.
Well then, I'll begin.{p}

Everyone, would you look at that branch up high?
You can see one thick branch stretching out there, can't you?
That one, you see, is just right for hanging yourself.
Do you know what else this cherry tree is called?
It's called the 'Hanging Cherry.'{p}Do you know why?
Someone hanged themselves from that branch
There's a rumor that if you hang yourself from that branch, you go to heaven
I don't know

It's true that, in the past, quite a few people have hanged themselves from this cherry tree.
But not one of them died of their own free will.
They are chosen by the cherry tree.
You think I'm lying, don't you?
I'm not.
This cherry tree, you see, chooses one sacrifice every year.
Of its own will.
Of course, I doubt anyone has ever heard that someone hangs themselves from this tree every year.
{a}{f:|}, you and Fukuzawa are only first-years, so it's natural that you wouldn't know, but...
Besides, even if the school tried to hide a rumor like that, it couldn't.
It would be bound to spread.
A school where, every single year without fail, someone hangs themselves from the cherry tree... imagine that.
Creepy, isn't it?{p}
If you'd known about a rumor like that, you wouldn't have come to this school, would you?
That has nothing to do with it
No, I wouldn't have come

Exactly.
That's why nobody knows.{p}

Strange, isn't it?
Do you know why?
It's because the cherry tree buries the people who became its sacrifices beneath itself, all on its own.
That's why the bodies are never found.
Even so, the fact that someone has gone missing would remain, wouldn't it?
And yet no one ever finds out.
No one is surprised.
Not the teachers, not their friends, not their families: not a single person worries.
Why do you think that is?
The very existence of the sacrifice vanishes from everyone's minds.
In other words, for some reason, the person's whole past, every fact of the life they lived, is completely erased.{p}

Heh heh...
It becomes as though they never existed in the first place.
That's why no one notices.
That's why no one worries.{p}

After all, no one knows anything about such a person.
Now, don't you want to know why the cherry tree needs sacrifices?{p}Aren't you interested, {a}{f:|}?
I'm interested
I'm not interested

I despise liars.
I like honest people.
This cherry tree, you see, used to be a meeting place for couples.
This was decades ago now.{p}

And it was said that a couple who kissed beneath this cherry tree and swore their love to each other would be bound together forever.
Back then, it didn't yet have such a hateful nickname as the Hanging Cherry.
It was a symbol of happiness that bound two lovers together.
At that time, there was a couple named Kunio Hirooka and Hatsuko Orihara.
They, too, believed in the legend of the cherry tree, and dreamed that someday they would kiss beneath it and be bound by eternal love.
But you know, legends like that aren't made only of happy stories.
There was a dark side, too.{p}

It's cleverly made, isn't it?
If eternal love came that easily, the legend would lose all its value.
That's why you hardly ever heard of a couple who had put the legend to the test, not even as a rumor.
Perhaps there were actually many of them.
Everyone was so pure that they were too shy to talk about it, and if they did talk and then broke up, they'd be a real laughingstock, wouldn't they?
Secrets like that, you see, were kept between the two of them alone.
So Hirooka and Orihara told no one either, and waited for the time to come.{p}

Back then, making that kind of confession was the man's job.
These days so many men are spineless that the women seem to be the strong ones.
Around the time the cherry blossoms bloomed, Hirooka finally made up his mind.
He would perform the legendary ritual beneath the cherry tree in full bloom.
"...Orihara. If you don't mind, would you come with me, just the two of us, under those cherry blossoms?"
You understand what it meant when he said the two of them would go there, don't you?
Orihara blushed and gave a small nod.
How happy Hirooka was at that moment...
I can picture it as plainly as if it were right in front of me.
And so he asked her.
"When would be good for you?"{p}What do you think Orihara answered?
On the night of the next full moon
Early tomorrow morning
I'll leave it up to you

"On the night of the next full moon. I think that's just when the cherry blossoms will be in full bloom. Then..."
The two held hands and gazed into each other's eyes.
No more words were needed.
Though anyone who has never been in love wouldn't understand.
Do you understand, I wonder?
...And so, at last, the night of the full moon arrived.
As the day drew closer and closer, their hearts pounded and fluttered.
On the day itself, knowing that tonight was the night, they were so shy that whenever their eyes met during the day, they couldn't help looking away.{p}

At ten o'clock on the night of the full moon, the two met at the school's back gate.
It was a quiet night, without a soul around.
Of course, both of them had sneaked out of their homes.
If they'd told their families the truth, they would never have been allowed to go.
"Have you been waiting long?"
"No, I just got here."
Though each was sure the other would come, they had both been uneasy until they reached the back gate.
When they spotted each other, they ran to each other at the same moment and took each other's hands.
And they nodded together.
It was a signal to confirm their resolve.{p}

Then they passed alongside the old school building in the night and headed for that cherry tree.
The two of them could clearly feel their clasped hands growing damp with sweat.
However hard they tried not to notice, they could plainly hear their own hearts beating.
And even each other's.{p}

Can you believe it? Someone had come to the cherry tree before them.
And at the very moment they were kissing, no less.
If the legend was true, misfortune would now fall upon that couple.
"Ah!"
And before they could stop themselves, Hirooka and Orihara cried out.{p}

The pair nestled together, hidden in the cherry tree's silhouette, broke off their kiss in surprise.
And they looked around.
Hirooka and Orihara squeezed each other's hands tight.
At this rate, they would be found.{p}What do you think the two of them did?
They ran away
They stepped out to explain what had happened

"Let's run!"
Hirooka grabbed her hand and broke into a run on the spot.
"Wait! Please, wait!"
A man's voice called out behind them.
But they didn't turn around.
It was a mournful voice, one that seemed to drape itself over their backs.
But the two of them were too frightened to look back.{p}

And before they knew it, they had reached a nearby park.
"...What do we do?"
Orihara looked as if she might burst into tears at any moment.
Those people might hate them for this.
It had only been moonlight, but perhaps they had even seen their faces.
Thinking about it, she was so frightened that her tears overflowed and wouldn't stop.{p}What do you think Hirooka said to her then?
Let's find them tomorrow and apologize
It's not our fault, so don't let it bother you
Let's keep this a secret between the two of us and say nothing

"I couldn't see their faces. Could you, Orihara?"
Hirooka asked anxiously.
She only shook her head quietly.
At that, he made his decision.
He would keep quiet.
"Let's keep this a secret between just the two of us. That way, they're sure to convince themselves they were mistaken about seeing us.
And then they won't have to suffer any misfortune, will they?"
By saying so, Hirooka convinced himself as well.
In fact, perhaps that really was the best thing.
Orihara, too, decided to go along with Hirooka.
And so the two of them came to share a secret.
Having a secret of your own, just between two people, is important, you know.
When a man and a woman share a secret, their relationship moves forward quickly.
Perhaps the legend of the cherry tree was born from that very idea in the first place.
And then they parted, promising that tomorrow night, without fail, they would confirm their love once more.{p}

By now, their eyes showed that they trusted each other completely.
Perhaps seeing another couple's kiss had, if anything, deepened the bond between them.
And it seemed that things would go well for the two of them.
But...{p}

The next day, a young man and woman were found hanged from the cherry tree, dead.
There was no suicide note.
They had died tied to each other with rope, so that their bodies wouldn't come apart.
Still in each other's arms.
Hirooka thought to himself.
The ones who had died must surely be the couple the two of them had seen.
They must have despaired that misfortune would come because their kiss had been seen, and turned to thoughts of suicide.
If they couldn't be together in this world, they would find happiness in heaven: that was what they had vowed.
Is that hard for you to believe?
Do you think it's ridiculous to die over something like that?
But you know, people in the old days took love very seriously.
Heh heh heh... though you may not understand that.
Orihara felt just the same way Hirooka did.{p}
That night, the two of them met at the same time and in the same place as the night before.{p}

Even so, they found it hard to go to the cherry tree.
As for carrying out that legend, they were in no mood for anything of the kind.
Still, when they thought of the two who had died believing they'd been seen, they couldn't bear to be alone.
"...It's my fault. Because I ran away that time, they died. ...If I'd explained what happened then, those two might not have had to die."
Head bowed, Hirooka spoke weakly.
Orihara just cried in silence.
To be honest, the two of them had no idea what they should do from then on.
And that was when it happened.{p}

Suddenly, a voice called out to the two of them.
Not a voice they could clearly hear with their ears, but one that called directly inside their heads.
At first they were startled, thinking someone somewhere was watching them.
But they couldn't sense anyone there.
And then, this time, they heard it clearly.{p}

"You two killed them."
That was what the voice said, full of resentment.
Both of them were trembling so hard in the legs that they couldn't move.
The voice pressed on, as if to drive the point home.
"Because you saw them, two young lives were lost. If you had not had such wicked thoughts, time would have flowed on in peace. If you truly feel responsible, then let us see you take that so-called responsibility."
The voice was overbearing.
A heavy, oppressive voice without a shred of kindness in it.
The two hung their heads and fell silent.
The voice was demanding that they take responsibility.{p}What would you say?
I'll take responsibility
There's no need to take responsibility
I don't want to talk to the likes of you

I see.
You're surprisingly innocent, aren't you?
The two of them gave that answer, too.
Their consciences must have been tormenting them terribly.
"...It's true, I'm the one to blame. If I can, I want to take responsibility. ...What should I do?"
That was the answer Hirooka gave, I'm afraid.
The voice that replied sounded pleased.{p}
That voice belonged to the spirit that lives in that cherry tree.{p}

Urged on by the voice, the two of them walked unsteadily to the foot of the cherry tree.
The voice went on.
"...You, too, came here because you believed in my legend, did you not? Then, before you take responsibility, I shall grant the two of you eternal love. Now, exchange a kiss."
Out of nowhere, the cherry tree spirit said that.
What would you do?{p}Would you do as the voice says?
Do as it says
Don't do as it says
Run away
"Aaagh!"
"Eeeek!"{p}

Suddenly, four hands shot up out of the earth.
The hands seized the two of them firmly by the ankles.
When the two looked down at their feet in shock, the soil squirmed and heaved up, and two faces emerged from it.
They were, without a doubt, the faces of the two who had been found hanged.
"This is what it means to take responsibility."
The cherry tree spirit said it coldly.
And then the two of them were dragged down into the earth, just like that.
"You have sworn eternal love. But eternity is fragile and fleeting. If you wish to keep it for all eternity, bring me one sacrifice every year..."
Those were the last words the two of them ever heard.{p}

{a}{f:|}, the hands came out of the ground right about where you're standing now.
They came out from around there.
Heh heh heh heh...
This is the true story behind this tree.
Even now, Hirooka and Orihara offer up one sacrifice every year so they can keep their eternal love.{p}
Now, I wonder who it will be this year?{p}{a}{f:|}, it might be you, don't you think?
Say the story is a lie
Say we should go back to the club room now

A lie?
You're saying my story is a lie?
Why?
It isn't a lie.
If you say things like that, you'll get yourself killed.
You'll be cursed.
No, you're already cursed.{p}
You're a cursed child.{p}Ah ha ha ha ha...
Tell her to stop and grab her
Ignore her

What are you doing?
...Stop that, would you?{p}

Heh heh heh heh...
You moved, didn't you?
Do you remember your promise to me?
I told you not to move until my story was over, didn't I?
My story isn't over yet.
And yet you broke your promise.
You see, I absolutely hate it when people break their promises to me.
And so does the cherry tree spirit.
Because you broke your promise, I've been set free.
So I'll tell you.{p}

...The truth is, every year, the student who's to become the sacrifice always has a dream.
A dream of Hirooka and Orihara.
And that's how they learn the legend of the cherry tree.
And that they're going to be the sacrifice, too.
Within a week of the dream, the dreamer is called away, they say.
Lured by the two of them, the dreamer hangs themselves while asleep, apparently.
Yes, this year, the one who had the dream was me.
That's why I know.
The legend of the cherry tree.
And in that dream, they taught me all sorts of things.
That there was just one single way for me to save myself.{p}

It's to make someone else take your place.
Anyone will do: you tell them the story of the cherry tree you saw in your dream.
When you do, you make them promise not to scream and not to move from where they are.
Then, if they break that promise, they become your substitute.{p}

Because I still want to live, for a long, long time.
I want to enjoy my life.
For that, I'll do anything.
{a}{f:|}, you'll have the dream soon, too.
The dream of the cherry tree.
When that happens, make sure you remember that you had it.
And then, within a week, tell someone.
If you do, this time that person will take your place.
If you die, I'll grieve for you.
...But that's impossible, isn't it?
If you die, no one will know you ever existed.
Your very existence will vanish from this world, after all.
Even if I wanted to grieve for you, I couldn't.
...Good luck, {a}{f:|}.
Don't hold it against me.
Just think of it as fate...{p}

I'm sorry, but this is a story I can only tell to people who've made me that promise.
As for why, you'd only understand that by hearing the story itself, so I can't explain it to you.
That's how frightening a story it is.
So, I'm afraid I can't tell it to you.
But if you ever want to hear it, let me know.
When you do, don't be shy. Just say, "I promise, so please tell me."
I'll tell it to you anytime.
So that's as far as my story goes...
Now, shall we go back to the club room?{p}

That's right, it's just as the name says.
Exactly that.
Simple, isn't it?
But you know, the story of this cherry tree isn't as simple as you all think.{p}

I've heard that rumor before, too.
If I remember right, someone tried to hang themselves from that cherry tree, but survived.
And I heard that while they were unconscious, they had a near-death experience.
Apparently they got within one step of heaven, but, well, a rumor is just a rumor.
Anyway, it's just as the name says.
Yes, the Hanging Cherry...
But you know, the story of this cherry tree isn't as simple as you all think.{p}

So you're saying you don't need to hear my story anymore?
I see...
But you know, at the start you promised me you wouldn't move until my story was over.
If I stop my story here, you'll never be able to move from this spot.
You're laughing like that, but...{p}

Heh heh heh.
I'll tell you something good.{p}

Hirooka flew into a rage.
And who could blame him?
If anyone saw the ritual, the couple would meet a miserable end.
On impulse, Hirooka ran straight at the girl.
Not that he had any purpose in mind.
His head was simply in turmoil.
And Hirooka caught the girl.{p}

"Why did you have to look?!
If it weren't for you, it would've worked!"
Before he knew it, Hirooka was choking the girl by the neck.
"S-stop it!"
At Orihara's voice, Hirooka came to his senses and noticed the girl hanging limp in his arms.
She wasn't breathing.
What a terrible thing he had done.{p}

"Wh-what do we do?"
Orihara asked in a trembling voice.
Seeing her so frightened, Hirooka hit on an idea.
To secretly bury the girl beneath the cherry tree.
He couldn't bear for Orihara to become an accomplice to murder, and he couldn't bear being caught and separated from her, either.
Orihara was shocked by Hirooka's proposal.
But in the end, she decided to help.
That's what a woman in love is like, isn't it?{p}

Working together, the two of them somehow managed to bury the girl.
It's a strange thing, but it felt as though cooperating like that had made the bond between them stronger.{p}

But some time after that, Hirooka started acting strange.
He grew distant somehow, and avoided Orihara.
They'd always gone home together, but now he'd vanish on his own.
Puzzled, Orihara tried to ask him about it.
But he just evaded her questions.
The girl had been declared missing, so there should have been nothing to worry about.{p}

Then one day after school, Orihara followed Hirooka.
And what do you know, he went to that cherry tree.
What could he be up to?
Orihara drew closer, and the next moment she felt as if she'd been doused with ice water.{p}
Why? Because the one waiting for him beneath the cherry tree was the girl who should have been dead.{p}

Hirooka happily took the girl in his arms.
And then he kissed her.
Orihara was shaken.
Not so much because the dead girl was there, but because Hirooka had kissed someone else.
So before she knew it, she rushed out.
Lunging at him, she shoved Hirooka hard in the back.{p}

Caught off guard, Hirooka staggered and slammed his head hard against the cherry tree.
There was a dull, sickening sound.{p}

When Hirooka fell, the trunk of the cherry tree was smeared thick with blood.
...He must have hit it in just the wrong spot.
Hirooka was dead.
As Orihara stood there dumbstruck, the girl jeered and laughed at her.
"Serves you right! That's your punishment for killing me. As if I'd let you two be the only ones who get to be happy!"
With a shrill laugh, the girl melted away and vanished.
But by then, Orihara could no longer hear a thing.
Killing her beloved Hirooka must have been an unbearable shock.{p}

...The next day, Orihara was found dead, hanging from a branch of the cherry tree.
At her feet, they say, Hirooka's body had been laid out.{p}

This is the true story behind this tree.
But actually, there's more to it.
The two of them, who in the end were brought to misery just as the legend said, became evil spirits, they say.
And it seems they convinced themselves that if they offered sacrifices to this tree, their love would surely be fulfilled.
Ever since then, every year, one person dies beneath this cherry tree.
As a sacrifice for the love of Orihara and Hirooka.{p}

"Maybe we should explain what happened..."
"Yes, maybe we should..."
The two of them started walking toward the other couple.
The other pair seemed shaken, too, and even by moonlight alone, the two could sense it.
Each time that wave of agitation reached them from the other side, their steps grew heavier.
It was Hirooka who finally couldn't stand the situation any longer.{p}

"I wish we hadn't run away back then. If I was going to regret it this much, I should have apologized right then..."
Then Hirooka told Orihara that tomorrow they should find the other couple and apologize.
She agreed with him, saying that would be best.
The two of them would find the couple tomorrow and apologize.
And they parted, promising that the following night, at last, they would once again confirm their love for each other.{p}

"It was an unfortunate thing, sure, but it's not our fault. Besides, if we'd been a little earlier, we might have been the ones who got seen."
At Hirooka's words, Orihara's face stiffened.
"B-but... then I feel so sorry for those two..."
"Orihara! You matter more to me than some people I don't even know. Let's just forget about it."
The more fervently Hirooka spoke, the more Orihara's face stiffened.
"The Hirooka I love isn't that kind of person. Let's go back and apologize."
When Orihara pressed him, Hirooka reluctantly nodded.
And so they went back to the cherry tree.{p}

......But it was already too late.
Beneath the cherry tree, a boy and a girl lay dead.
They must have been afraid of the misfortune to come.
Two bodies lit by the moonlight, lovingly holding hands.
Orihara's heart filled with regret.
If it was going to come to this, they should never have run.
But Hirooka, it seems, was thinking about something else.
"If anyone finds us here, we're done for. Let's hurry home."
Orihara couldn't believe her ears.
But Hirooka just turned and briskly started for home.{p}

"W-wait!"
Just as Orihara started to go after him...
There was a strange swishing, slithering sound.{p}

When she turned around, the branches of the cherry tree were writhing like whips!
The branches came at Orihara like living things with wills of their own.
"Help me!"
Orihara clung to Hirooka.
And Hirooka shoved her away.
"You'll get me caught, too!"
In that instant, Orihara felt she understood who Hirooka really was.
That he cared only about himself, that as long as he was saved, nothing else mattered.
And then, somehow, all her strength drained away.
She felt like a fool for having loved such a man.
Orihara stopped where she stood, and the cherry tree wrapped around her neck and squeezed.
And whip-like branches shot out at the fleeing Hirooka's neck, too.
A branch went straight through Hirooka's throat.{p}

That is the story behind this tree.
{a}{f:|}, you of all people should understand, shouldn't you?
The grudge that surrounds this tree, and the lingering attachment to this world.
You understand, don't you?
Go on, come closer and take a good look at the trunk.{p}

I heard laughter right beside me.
It was Iwashita.
Iwashita was looking down at {f:me|me} triumphantly.
You moved, didn't you.
That means you've broken your vow.
You see, I had been chosen as this tree's sacrifice.
Perhaps because it bathed in so much human blood, this cherry tree came to crave sacrifices.{p}

When this tree appeared in my dream and said it would make me its sacrifice, I wondered what would become of me.
So I cast a charm.
One that would pass the cherry tree's curse on to anyone who made a promise with me and then broke it.
It could have been anyone, but I thought this was the perfect opportunity.
There. Now I'm free.
Thank you, {a}{f:|}.
I don't know when it will be, but when you become this tree's sacrifice, I'll at least light some incense for you.
After all, you saved my life.
Heh heh...
Now, shall we go back to the newspaper club room?{p}

"That couldn't be helped! So there's no reason for us to take responsibility!"
Hirooka blurted it out in a forceful tone.
That overbearing voice must have made his blood boil before he knew it.
He hardly seemed like the meek Hirooka of a moment ago...
He was always calm and never spoke so forcefully, so she seemed a little startled.
Then, unexpectedly, the voice said,
"...I see. The young are quick to get heated.
I will give you time.
I will not say how long. Reflect on what you did.
And when you are ready to take responsibility, come here again.
You must come. I warn you, running is useless.
I am always watching you."
That's what it said.{p}

"Anyway, we have to get out of here!"
He took her hand and ran.{p}

Before they knew it, the two of them had run quite a long way from the school.
"We should be all right now."
Then they walked on, neither of them saying a word...
It was he who broke the silence first, unable to bear it any longer.
"Orihara. Let's forget what happened under that cherry tree tonight. From tomorrow on, we must never talk about it, not even when we're alone together. It was a dream. We have to forget it, and quickly."
She nodded.
Then he walked her home.
At her front door, she let go of his hand reluctantly and closed the door.
After a sleepless night, morning began again as if nothing had happened.
The harder they tried not to think about that night, the more it gnawed at them.
Even when they were together, things were awkward between them, and it was no fun at all...
And so the days went by.{p}

Then, after school exactly one week after that night, he worked up the nerve to talk to her.
"I'm sorry to bring this up again myself after what I said, but..."
"It's all right. It's been bothering me too, so much that I can't sleep at night. I was just about to bring it up myself."
It seems both of them had been dying to talk about that night.
"I'm thinking of going back to that cherry tree once more. I have something in mind, too...
And the cherry tree did say we must come... What will you do, Orihara?"
"...I'll go too. I don't think there's anything to worry about as long as you're with me, Hirooka... I really don't think that voice was a dream. I wonder if maybe it was the voice of that cherry tree..."
And so they decided to meet at the back gate at ten o'clock that night.{p}

For some reason, this time both of them reached the school gate before the agreed time.
Then they walked around behind the old school building.
A waning moon lit the surroundings with its feeble light.
Fukuzawa mentioned it earlier, didn't she?
The cherry tree was just a little past full bloom, at its most beautiful moment, as the petals fell.{p}
